title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on Compensation, etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement
title_original: 5ㆍ18민주화운동 관련자 보상 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON COMPENSATION, ETC. FOR PERSONS RELATED TO THE MAY 18 DEMOCRATIZATION MOVEMENT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Compensation, etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on June 30, 2006>

Article 1-2 (Diseases Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement)
The term "diseases prescribed by Presidential Decree" in item (c) of subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on Compensation, etc. for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means diseases newly arising or aggravated due directly or indirectly to injury, being wanted by investigative authorities, arrest, detention, or similar circumstances related to the May 18 Democratization Movement, which the Compensation Deliberation Committee for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Compensation Deliberation Committee") recognizes as such diseases.

Article 2 (Composition of Compensation Support Committee)
(1) The members of the Compensation Support Committee for Persons Related to the May 18 Democratization Movement under Article 3 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Compensation Support Committee") shall be the following persons: <Amended on December 7, 2021; December 30, 2025>
1. The Minister of Finance and Economy, Minister of Justice, Minister of the Interior and Safety, Minister of Health and Welfare, Minister of Employment and Labor, Minister of Planning and Budget, and Minister of Government Legislation;
2. Persons of extensive learning and experience commissioned by the Prime Minister in consideration of gender.
(2) The vice-chairperson of the Compensation Support Committee shall be the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended on December 23, 1994; June 30, 2006; December 31, 2008; December 30, 2025>
(3) Commissioned members of the Compensation Support Committee shall serve two-year terms and may be reappointed only once. <Newly Inserted on June 29, 2023>

Article 3 (Duties of Chairperson of Compensation Support Committee, etc.)
(1) The chairperson of the Compensation Support Committee shall represent the Committee and exercise general supervision over its affairs. <Amended on January 5, 2021>
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform duties due to an accident, the vice-chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf.

Article 4 (Meetings of Compensation Support Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Compensation Support Committee shall convene and preside over its meetings.
(2) A meeting shall commence with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, including the chairperson, and a resolution shall be adopted by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.

Article 5 (Administrative Staff of Compensation Support Committee)
(1) The Compensation Support Committee shall have one secretary and other necessary staff to handle its affairs.
(2) The chairperson shall appoint the secretary and staff from among public officials belonging to the Ministry of the Interior and Safety; the secretary shall be a general-service public official belonging to the Senior Executive Service. <Amended on June 12, 2006; June 30, 2006; December 31, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
(3) The secretary shall manage the Committee's affairs under the chairperson's direction and may attend and speak at meetings of the Committee.

Article 6 (Composition of Compensation Deliberation Committee)
(1) The members of the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall be the following persons: <Amended on December 7, 2021; June 23, 2026>
1. The president of Chonnam National University, the Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City, the chief prosecutor of the Gwangju District Prosecutors' Office, the superintendent of education of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City, the head of the Gwangju Regional Employment and Labor Office, and two chairpersons of the subcommittees under Article 4 (4) of the Act;
2. Persons of extensive learning and experience commissioned by the Prime Minister in consideration of gender.
(2) The vice-chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall be the superintendent of education of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City. <Amended on June 30, 2006; December 7, 2021; June 23, 2026>
(3) Commissioned members of the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall serve two-year terms and may be reappointed only once. <Newly Inserted on June 29, 2023>

Article 7 (Operation of Compensation Deliberation Committee, etc.)
Articles 3 through 5 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the duties of the chairperson, meetings, and administrative staff of the Compensation Deliberation Committee. In such cases, references to the "Compensation Support Committee" shall be deemed references to the "Compensation Deliberation Committee"; references to the "chairperson of the Compensation Support Committee" shall be deemed references to the "chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee"; references to "public officials belonging to the Ministry of the Interior and Safety" shall be deemed references to "public officials belonging to Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City"; and references to a "general-service public official belonging to the Senior Executive Service" shall be deemed references to a "local government administrative secretary (Grade IV)." <Amended on June 12, 2006; June 30, 2006; December 31, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; June 23, 2026>

Article 8 (Composition of Subcommittees)
(1) The Compensation Deliberation Committee shall have a subcommittee for reviewing whether persons are related to the movement, which performs the duties under Article 4 (2) 1 of the Act, and a subcommittee for determining disability grades, which performs the duties under Article 4 (2) 2 of the Act.
(2) Each subcommittee shall consist of no more than ten members commissioned by the chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee; the chairperson of each subcommittee shall be elected from among its members.
(3) Matters necessary for the operation of the subcommittees shall be determined by the chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee following a resolution of that Committee.

Article 9 (Allowances for Committee Members and Travel Expenses for Witnesses, etc.)
(1) Allowances may be paid within budgetary limits to members attending meetings of the Compensation Support Committee, Compensation Deliberation Committee, and subcommittees.
(2) Travel expenses and actual expenses may be paid within budgetary limits to witnesses or reference witnesses appearing before the committees under Article 18 of the Act.

Article 10 (Application of Average Wages)
(1) Where reliable proof cannot be presented under Article 5 (3) of the Act, the average wages to be used instead shall be based on monthly wages or daily labor wages according to nationwide statistics for men and women by occupation, compiled by an agency conducting wage surveys and periodically publishing wage statistics at least once each year: Provided, That where nationwide statistics are unavailable, monthly wages or daily labor wages based on regional statistics for Gwangju Metropolitan City shall apply.
(2) The average wages under paragraph (1) shall first be based on reliable statistics of construction wage rates; where such statistics are unavailable, statistics from the Survey Report on Actual Wages by Occupation published by the Ministry of Employment and Labor shall apply; and where those statistics are also unavailable, monthly wages or daily labor wages by gender surveyed by another reliable method shall apply: Provided, That the minimum wage for purposes of this paragraph shall be the 1980 average wage across all industries by gender, based on the Survey Report on Actual Wages by Occupation published by the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on July 12, 2010; January 5, 2021>

Article 11 (Deduction of Living Expenses)
When calculating compensation for surviving family members under Article 5 (4) of the Act, living expenses shall be deducted from monthly wages, monthly actual earnings, or average wages in accordance with attached Table 1.

Article 12 (Employable Periods, Grades of Physical Disability, and Rates of Loss of Working Capacity, etc.)
(1) The employable period under Article 5 (5) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 2; grades of physical disability and rates of loss of working capacity shall be as specified in attached Table 3.
(2) Where there are two affected parts of the body, a grade for each part shall be determined in accordance with attached Table 3 and then a comprehensive assessment grade shall be determined in accordance with attached Table 4.
(3) Where at least three parts of the body are affected, a comprehensive assessment grade shall first be determined for the two most seriously affected parts in accordance with attached Table 4; that grade and the next most seriously affected part shall then be comprehensively reassessed in accordance with attached Table 4 to determine a grade.
(4) Where at least three of the most seriously affected body parts are individually assessed as Grade 14 under attached Table 3, Grade 13 under attached Table 3 shall apply.

Article 13 (Medical Support Payments)
Medical support payments for future medical treatment costs, nursing care expenses, purchase of assistive devices, etc. under Article 6 (1) of the Act shall be calculated by the following methods: <Amended on December 7, 2021>
1. Future medical treatment costs shall be the amount calculated based on an estimate of treatment costs issued by a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a medical college in the Republic of Korea (excluding a branch hospital), or a hospital designated by the Compensation Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as a "designated hospital, etc."): Provided, That where a designated hospital, etc. acknowledges the need for future treatment but cannot estimate its costs, the amount shall be determined by the Compensation Deliberation Committee in consideration of the opinions of the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee and future treatment costs in comparable cases;
2. Nursing care expenses shall, where a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc. recognizes that a person related to the movement, after recovery, has a physical disability making it difficult to act without another person's care, be the product of 190,000 won per month and the average remaining life expectancy prescribed in attached Table 5;
3. Expenses for purchasing assistive devices shall, where a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc. recognizes a need to wear an assistive device, be the purchase price multiplied by the number of purchases expected to be necessary during the average remaining life expectancy, based on the device's useful life.

Article 14 (Livelihood Support Payments)
Standards for payment of livelihood support funds under Article 7 of the Act shall be determined by the Compensation Support Committee.

Article 15 (Applications for Payment of Compensation, etc.)
(1) A person intending to apply for payment of compensation, medical support payments, or livelihood support funds under Article 8 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "compensation, etc.") shall submit the following documents (including electronic documents) to the Compensation Deliberation Committee: <Amended on March 17, 2004; June 12, 2006; November 2, 2010>
1. One application for payment of compensation, etc., in attached Form No. 1;
2. Deleted. <June 12, 2006>
3. One certificate of family relationship records concerning the relevant person or a certified copy of a removed family register (in the latter case only for the survivors of deceased, missing, or injured persons whose relationship cannot be verified by a certificate of family relationship records);
4. One form selecting a representative of surviving family members in attached Form No. 2 (only where such a representative has been selected);
5. One letter of attorney to receive compensation, etc., in attached Form No. 3 (only where applying by proxy due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances);
6. One certificate of occupation and monthly wages in attached Form No. 4 (only for wage earners);
7. One certificate of occupation and monthly actual earnings in attached Form No. 5 (only for persons earning business income);
8. One copy of other evidence supporting the grounds for application.
(2) Where at least two survivors of a deceased, missing, or injured person have equal priority in inheritance of property in applying for and receiving compensation, etc. under paragraph (1), they shall select a representative of surviving family members by a form in attached Form No. 2: Provided, That this shall not apply where the heirs of equal priority cannot reach agreement.
(3) Where a person intending to apply for compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) cannot apply or receive payment directly due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances, the person may appoint an agent by a letter of attorney to receive compensation, etc. in attached Form No. 3, verified by any of the following persons: <Amended on April 4, 2003>
1. The head of a diplomatic mission abroad, where the person has emigrated or resides abroad;
2. The head of the relevant medical institution, where the person is hospitalized;
3. The head of the relevant detention institution, where the person is confined in a correctional institution or similar place;
4. The head of a Si, Gun, or Gu, in other cases.
(4) Where an application for payment of compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) lacks related documents listed in the subparagraphs of that paragraph, the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall require the applicant to supplement the documents.
(5) Upon receiving an application for payment of compensation, etc. under paragraph (1), the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall verify the applicant's resident registration record through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant does not consent to the verification, the Committee shall require submission of the relevant document. <Amended on November 2, 2010>

Article 16 (Request for Re-examination, etc.)
Where special grounds exist, the chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee may request the relevant subcommittee to re-examine or re-determine an examination or determination made by a subcommittee under Article 8.

Article 17 (Decisions)
(1) Decisions on payment of compensation, etc. under Article 9 of the Act shall be based on reliable evidence.
(2) Where the Compensation Deliberation Committee decides on compensation, it shall prepare a compensation decision in attached Form No. 6 stating the following, and the members who attended the Committee's meeting shall sign and affix their seals:
1. The applicant's name, address, and resident registration number;
2. The operative part of the decision;
3. Reasons;
4. Date of the decision.

Article 18 (Notification)
Where the Compensation Deliberation Committee decides on compensation, it shall retain the original decision and serve the applicant with two authentic copies of the compensation decision and a notice of the decision in attached Form No. 7. Where the applicant has an agent, the documents shall be served on the agent and one copy of the compensation decision shall be served on the applicant. The original compensation decision may be retained as an electronic document or digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Amended on November 12, 2024>

Article 19 (Applications for Re-examination)
A person intending to apply for re-examination under Article 11 of the Act shall submit the following documents to the Compensation Deliberation Committee:
1. One application for re-examination in attached Form No. 8;
2. One medical certificate on physical (mental) disability in attached Form No. 9 issued by a designated hospital, etc. (only where the disability grade is contested);
3. One copy of other evidence supporting the grounds for re-examination.

Article 19-2 (Application for Reclassification Physical Examination, etc.)
(1) A person intending to undergo a reclassification physical examination under Article 11-2 (1) or (2) of the Act shall submit an application for reclassification physical examination and payment of compensation, etc. in attached Form No. 8-2 to the Compensation Deliberation Committee, accompanied by the following documents: <Amended on June 29, 2023>
1. One letter of attorney to receive compensation, etc. (only where applying by proxy due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances);
2. One certificate of occupation and monthly wages (only where the person concerned is a wage earner);
3. One certificate of occupation and monthly actual earnings (only where the person concerned earns business income);
4. One copy of other evidence supporting the grounds for application.
(2) Reclassification physical examinations shall be conducted at least once every quarter on dates determined by the chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee in consultation with the chairperson of the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee.
(3) An application for a reclassification physical examination shall be deemed dismissed in either of the following cases: <Amended on August 31, 2015>
1. Where the reclassification physical examination results in no change to the disability grade;
2. Where the applicant does not undergo the physical examination requested by the applicant without any of the following reasons:
(a) A natural disaster or other similar natural calamity has occurred;
(b) Movement is difficult due to hospitalization or treatment following surgery or other reasons;
(c) Another unavoidable circumstance makes it difficult to undergo the physical examination.
(4) Where it is difficult to determine whether the reason under paragraph (3) 2 (b) or (c) applies, the chairperson of the Compensation Deliberation Committee may require the person who must undergo the reclassification examination to submit a written explanation of the reason.

Article 20 (Consent and Requests for Payment)
An applicant who receives notice of a compensation decision under the first sentence of Article 18 and intends to receive compensation, etc. shall submit a written consent and request in attached Form No. 10, accompanied by the following documents, to the Compensation Deliberation Committee: <Amended on November 12, 2024>
1. One authentic copy of the compensation decision;
2. One certificate of the applicant's registered seal impression or certificate of personal signature confirmation;
3. One copy of the bank passbook for the applicant's deposit account.

Article 20-2 (Payment after Deduction from Compensation, etc.)
The amount to be deducted from compensation, etc. under Article 16 (2) of the Act shall be the present value of amounts already received as compensation or damages under the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements or the State Compensation Act, calculated by applying the consumer price index annually designated and publicly notified by the Commissioner of the National Data Agency under subparagraph 2 of Article 3 of the Statistics Act. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 20-3 (Operation and Entrustment of Counseling and Treatment Programs for Victims of Sexual Violence)
(1) Under Article 19-2 (1) of the Act, the State shall establish and implement a plan to operate counseling and treatment programs in consideration of the characteristics and circumstances of victims of sexual violence, and shall record and retain details of counseling and treatment provided.
(2) Where the State intends to entrust the operation of counseling and treatment programs under Article 19-2 (2) of the Act, it shall select an entrusted institution from among medical institutions designated for treatment of sexual violence victims under Article 27 (1) of the Act on the Prevention of Sexual Violence and Protection, etc. of Victims, considering the institution's expertise, personnel, facilities, location, etc.
(3) Where the State entrusts duties to an institution selected under paragraph (2), it shall publicly notify the entrusted institution and the duties entrusted to it in the Official Gazette.
(4) The State may support the expenses necessary where it has entrusted duties to an institution selected under paragraph (2).

Article 20-4 (Support for Foundations Related to May 18 Democratization Movement, etc.)
(1) Under Article 21-2 (1) of the Act, the State and local governments may make contributions or provide support for the operating and project expenses of foundations conducting the following:
1. Projects to commemorate and memorialize the May 18 Democratization Movement;
2. Welfare projects for persons related to the May 18 Democratization Movement and their surviving family members;
3. Cultural and academic projects relating to the May 18 Democratization Movement;
4. Other projects relating to the May 18 Democratization Movement, as specified in the foundation's articles of incorporation.
(2) A foundation seeking contributions or support under Article 21-2 (1) of the Act shall submit the following documents to the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City: <Amended on June 23, 2026>
1. Its articles of incorporation;
2. Minutes of the board of directors' meetings for the relevant year, including budgets and statements of settlement of accounts;
3. A business plan.

Article 21 (Payment of Other Support Funds, etc.)
(1) The term "persons deemed to require support for their livelihood in connection with the May 18 Democratization Movement" in Article 22 (1) of the Act means persons recognized as having been unable to engage in an occupation or other livelihood activity due to their active participation in the May 18 Democratization Movement: Provided, That persons who have received a decision on payment of compensation, etc. under Article 9 of the Act shall be excluded. <Amended on May 29, 1993; June 30, 2006>
(2) A person seeking payment of other support funds shall submit an application for payment of other support funds in attached Form No. 11, accompanied by supporting documents substantiating the grounds for application, to the Compensation Deliberation Committee between July 1 and December 31, 2023. <Amended on May 29, 1993; June 30, 2006; August 31, 2015; June 29, 2023>
(3) Within 120 days from receiving an application for payment of other support funds, the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall deliberate and decide whether to pay and the amount, prepare a decision on payment of other support funds in attached Form No. 12, and have the attending members sign and seal it.
(4) Upon deciding whether to pay other support funds, the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall retain the original decision and serve the applicant with a notice of the decision in attached Form No. 13 and two authentic copies of the decision. Where the applicant has an agent, the documents shall be served on the agent and one copy of the decision shall be served on the applicant. The original decision may be retained as an electronic document or digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Amended on November 12, 2024>
(5) Where the Compensation Deliberation Committee rejects payment of compensation, etc. under Article 9 of the Act and finds that the requirements under paragraph (1) are met, it may decide to pay other support funds even without a separate application therefor.
(6) An applicant notified of a decision on payment of other support funds under paragraph (4) who wishes to receive them shall submit a request for payment of other support funds in attached Form No. 14, accompanied by the following documents, to the Compensation Deliberation Committee: <Amended on July 30, 2024>
1. One authentic copy of the decision on payment of other support funds;
2. One certificate of the applicant's registered seal impression or certificate of personal signature confirmation.
(7) The standards for payment of other support funds and other necessary payment matters shall be determined by the Compensation Support Committee.

Article 22 (Payment Agency)
Compensation, etc. and other support funds decided by the Compensation Deliberation Committee shall be paid by the Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City. <Amended on June 30, 2006; June 23, 2026>

Article 23 (Time of Payment)
Compensation, etc. and other support funds shall be paid within 15 days from the date of a request for payment under Article 20 or Article 21 (6).

Article 24 (Public Notice)
On the date this Decree enters into force, the Mayor of Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City shall publicly announce in the Official Gazette the following matters concerning applications for payment of compensation, etc. and other support funds and shall also announce them in at least two daily newspapers, public bulletins, Internet websites, broadcasts, or other media: <Amended on June 30, 2006; November 24, 2020; June 23, 2026>
1. Persons eligible for payment;
2. Qualifications of applicants;
3. Agencies receiving applications;
4. Application period;
5. Required documents;
6. Standards for calculating payment amounts;
7. Procedures for deliberation and decision;
8. Other matters necessary for application and payment.

Article 25 Deleted. <December 7, 2021>
